text: Maria G: quick design/a11y question — our ‘Stop Dedicated Pool’ modal CTA is pretty long and for screen readers it reads the whole paragraph after the button label. feels noisy. can we shorten the visible CTA and add an sr-only announcement for details? Alex F: yep saw that. current primary CTA: "Stop pool and migrate traffic (recommended)" — too wordy. suggest visible: "Stop pool" and add extra context for assistive tech. :thinking: Jordan P: agree. visible CTAs should be short verbs. for SR we can use aria-describedby pointing to a hidden text node that explains the consequences. also keyboard focus needs to remain on the modal. Samira K: proposed microcopy options — pick one? 1) Visible: "Stop pool"; SR-only: "This will stop the dedicated GPU pool and migrate new requests to the fallback tier. Existing in-flight requests will finish." 2) Visible: "Disable pool"; SR-only: "Disables the pool immediately; traffic will route to your fallback model variant. Billing for reserved capacity will continue until end of billing period." 3) Visible: "Deactivate"; SR-only: "Deactivating the pool removes reserved compute immediately; you can re-enable later from the Dedicated page." Maria G: i like option 1 but tweak the SR copy to be shorter and avoid billing language in the primary flow. maybe: "This stops the dedicated GPU pool.
